What is Quantum Immortality?

Quantum immortality is the concept that the nature of quantum mechanics is such that a given individual cannot die from their own subjective viewpoint. Basically, that the laws of physics say that you are immortal. Period.

Sounds neat, but there are downsides, right?

Yes there are. If quantum immortality is true, you cannot die from your perspective. That is the exact limit of its function. You can still get old. You can still loose limbs. You could still contract a virus that left you in excruciating agony for the rest of your existence. Most importantly, other people can still die from your perctive - and you can still die from theirs.

That sounds pretty unattractive.

Not a question, and not a question about it. Nature very rarely aligns to human aesthetics. If the world adhered to human ideas of beauty, then Plato would have been right in modelling the world in four Elements, or Ptolemy would have been right in the earth-centric odel of the solar system, or einstein would have been right when he said "God doesn't play dice". Our goal isn't to claim that heaven is the world and we live in it. Our goal is to examine, without cringing, the implications and reality of this idea. If that's not your cuppa, the back button is up and to the left. probably.

It is my cuppa, but before going any further, is this idea even falsifiable?

Of course! Like any good scientific hypothesis, QI can be disproved. Three infinities must not be present in the structure of the universe for this to be the case. If the extent of space is infinite, and the conditions we observe in our universe persist; if the extent of time is infinite, and cosomogony reccurs; if the fineness of scale is infnite, and the Many-Worlds interpretation is correct; if any of those conditions hold, QI is implied (we'll get to why shortly). If all three of those conditions are false, QI is also false, although lesser analogues might still be possible in any case where Many Worlds is true.

So how do those conditions "prove" QI, then?

They do not prove it. At our current level of knowledge, they imply it's truth. There might be deeper principles that we are not presently aware of that invalidate QI even if those conditions hold. Their complete absence, however, proves that QI is false.

That clarified, this is why they imply it.

Condition 1: Unbounded Space and Persistent Laws

Any system with a finite number of states eventually enters periodic behaviour. This is an anglicization of a mathematical theorem, also known as an absolute truth. It has important implications for all three conditions, but is especially relevant here. As it turns out, periodic behaviour in space and time are the same thing. In time, we just call it "periodic behaviour", eg, like a pendulum. In space, we call it a crystal. This can be extended to the extent of physical dimensions. In present physics, the concept of "outside of space" is incoherent; however, space can still be finite! All that happens is that it connects with itself at the edges. So, if the universe was a cube of space about the size of your fist, and it had a single marble in it, if you looked to either side of any of the 3D directions - foward, behind, up, down, left, right - you would see the same marble, separated by the distance of one fist in any of those directions.

This is a crystal, made of space instead of matter.

Any universe that has a finite extent in space is such a crystal. If this is the case, and the other two conditions are also false you are not immortal.

The reason why this invalidates quantum immortality is that it demonstrates, at a stroke, that the universe has a finite amount of matter. That means that nowhere in the universe is there guaranteed to be a copy of you down to the very same quantum information where events devolve differently, and a fatal event, isn't.

Uh. Wait, what?

The Infinite Universe

Just as a finite universe must be a crystal, an infinite universe must not be one. And a universe that is not a crystal is one of three things: random, irrationally chaotic, or a quasicrystal. Irrational chaos is a bit like the digits of pi; it goes on forever, and cannot be repeated. Quasicrystals are systems where some form of "order" is present, but which otherwise also do not become periodic. Penrose tiles are an excellent example of a simple system that exhibits quasicrystalline behaviours.

Regardless of which of these conditions attain the fact that they are mapped to a system of infinite size means that all patterns that can exist, do. And a human being is just a pattern of matter - if you believe otherwise, then presumably, you have beliefs that contradict QI in any case, and we're wasting our mutual time.

If all patterns exist, then there are an infinite number of copies of you in existence. There are also (contained in that infinite set) an infinite number of copies of you that experienced ever event, down to the subatomic scale, in exactly the same way. Their quantum information is exactly, 100% identical to yours. If you and one of those version of you were side by side, absolutely nothing would be able to distinguish them. This is because they are not versions of you. They are you.

Well, that sounds like periodic behaviour. WTF?

No, still not periodic. Pi doesn't repeat, but the sequence of numbers 14159 will occur in it's digits an infinite number of times. That's what's happening here. All of the copies of ourselves are 14159-analogies. The sequence is the same, but the surroundings aren't. In a universal sense, all of the events hve been the same, but there will come a point in time where divergence occurs. You and one of your spacially-dislocated copies will flip a coin, and due to some small, subatomic event, the nerve impulse will differ at some point in the chain, and you will get heads, and the copy will get tails, and the pseudoperiodicity will break down.

Incidentally, you don't have to worry about ever running out. This is a simplicifaction, but infinity divided by two is still infiity. If half of your copies split off, that just means that there are now two infinite sets.

The implication to quantum immortality is simple from here: "Infinite" probability that could kill an entire infiite set of you might or might not be possible, but before it even occurs, there are copies of you that split off when the probability of death was still finite. You can't percieve being any dead copies of yourself. Therefore, you will always percieve being one of the living ones. QED.

Condition 2: Unbounded Time and Eternal Recurrence

Consider a universe that is finite in space. Is it necessary that this universe is a crystal?

Well, actually, no, it isn't. Just as you can talk about crystals of space, physics recognizes the concept of crystals of time. Instead of a configuration of atoms repeating endlessly, a time crystal is a sequence of events repeating endlessly. This is one of those deeply unintuitive physical concepts, and I admit, I have yet to understand it sufficiently well to attempt a deep explanation of what it is. This section will be updated when I gain a clear enough understanding of what time crystals are to explain them properly (or when a physicist who already has such an idea contributes an explanation of sufficient brevity).

Condition 3: Unbounded Scale and Many Worlds

How does any of that have anything to do with the universe not letting me die?

That's the fun part; it doesn't. Not directly. Quantum Immortality is called that because of it's specific applications to us. What it really is, though, is just a special case of the anthropic principle.

The anthropic principle runs like this: Look at the universe. Why is it like that? Because it must be like that for you to be there asking that question.

It's easily one of the least intuitive arguments in science. The first time I saw it, I thought it wasn't even actually an argument, just a tautology. It isn't, though, because one thing that we do know about quantum mechanics is that the universe behaves probabalistically. At the moent of the big bang, there was no requirement that humans would evolve. That we exist means thatr we did, anyway.
